title: Lior and the Parish
premise: When a drowned man washes up in the river wearing clothes stolen from Odile Kavanagh's own closet, the insurance investigator's photographic memory becomes both their greatest asset and a target. The dead man is connected to a five-year-old fire at St. Brigid's parish — a fire Odile investigated and closed as accidental, though fragments of memory have always itched wrong. As the trial of the town's beloved deacon approaches, Odile discovers the key witness, a young man named Lior, was declared dead years ago but may be alive and hiding in plain sight among the parish's found-family network. To find Lior before the trial collapses, Odile must unravel their own falsified memories, confront the mentor who taught them to file secrets away, and choose between the law that employs them and the justice the town has quietly practiced for decades. In the end, Odile finds Lior living under the church itself, testifies to what they truly remember rather than what they were paid to record, and dismantles the cover-up — losing their career but gaining, at last, a family that chose them back.
about_author: Wendell Reyes is a former small-town court clerk who spent a decade transcribing other people's worst days before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about ordinary people who discover the paperwork of their lives has been lying to them.

chapters.title: The Wrong Clothes
chapters.summary: Odile Kavanagh, POV. A body surfaces in the Millbrook River wearing Odile's own gray overcoat and scarf, items stolen from their closet sometime in the past month. Odile catalogs every detail with unnerving precision while the sheriff watches them too closely. Emotional beat: cold dread beneath professional composure — the crime has reached inside their own home.

chapters.title: Filed Under F
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. At the office, Odile pulls their old file on the St. Brigid's parish fire and discovers pages subtly altered — dates shifted, a witness name inked over. Their photographic memory clashes with the paper record, proving someone edited history after the fact. Emotional beat: vertigo; the archive Odile trusted is a crime scene.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears He's Dead
chapters.summary: Sheriff Dana Pruitt, POV. Pruitt reveals the dead man is Tomas Reyes, once the parish handyman, officially killed in the fire five years ago. She warns Odile off: the trial of Deacon Ambrose Hale starts in six weeks, and the town wants it quiet. Emotional beat: institutional pressure wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. Digging into the fire inquest, Odile finds a single mention of a second survivor — a teenager named Lior Voss, declared dead by his guardian's affidavit. No body, no grave, no school records after that winter. Emotional beat: the first spark of obsession; a ghost with a paper trail.

chapters.title: Sunday Best
chapters.summary: Odile attends service at rebuilt St. Brigid's incognito. The congregation is a tight web of misfits and strays — the found family the parish shelters. Someone recognizes the coat Odile is wearing and goes pale. Emotional beat: warmth on the surface, surveillance underneath; Odile realizes they are being watched too.

chapters.title: What the Memory Keeps
chapters.summary: Odile, POV, flashback-laced. Reconstructing the night of the fire from raw sensory memory, Odile recalls a detail the official report erased: two silhouettes leaving the rectory before the flames, one carrying a child. Emotional beat: grief and self-doubt — can Odile trust a mind that remembers everything except what it was told to forget?

chapters.title: The Mentor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Odile visits retired investigator Marcus Bell, who trained them and signed off the original fire report. Bell is cagey, then frightened; he admits he was paid to close the case but won't say by whom. That night his house burns. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into guilt — Odile asked questions and someone answered with fire.

chapters.title: Ashes, Twice
chapters.summary: Pruitt, POV. Investigating Bell's death, Pruitt finds the same accelerant signature as the parish fire and must decide whether to protect her town or her conscience. She quietly shares evidence with Odile, breaking ranks. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance between two keepers of secrets.

chapters.title: Alphabet of Strangers
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. Cross-referencing five years of insurance claims, donations, and parish rosters, Odile maps the found family — and notices every member received anonymous payments timed to the fire anniversary. Someone has been buying silence, or gratitude. Emotional beat: the puzzle clicking together, and the loneliness of being outside every circle.

chapters.title: The Coat Thief
chapters.summary: Odile stakes out their own house and catches a gaunt young man breaking in — not to steal, but to return something: a photograph of Odile's mother at St. Brigid's. He flees when headlights sweep the street. Emotional beat: shock and tenderness entangled; the intruder knew Odile's family.

chapters.title: Mother's Pews
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. Confronting their estranged mother, Odile learns she once sang in the parish choir and that Lior Voss was her godson — the boy she begged Odile's firm not to erase from the record. Emotional beat: old wounds reopened; the case was never impersonal, it never was.

chapters.title: Deacon Hale's Hands
chapters.summary: Deacon Ambrose Hale, POV. Hale prays, prepares for trial, and we learn he knows exactly who died in the fire and why — and believes his sin was mercy. He recognizes Odile as a threat to the fragile peace he bought. Emotional beat: chilling sympathy for a man doing monstrous bookkeeping.

chapters.title: Six Weeks, Five Dead
chapters.summary: Pruitt, POV. The body count around the old case grows: Bell, a records clerk, a former sexton. Someone is cleaning witnesses faster than the defense can. Pruitt suspects the killer isn't protecting Hale but framing him. Emotional beat: rising panic; the trial is a fuse burning toward everyone.

chapters.title: Below the Sacristy
chapters.summary: Odile follows the photograph's clue to a sealed crypt beneath the church ruins and finds Lior Voss alive — grown, wary, keeping the parish's true ledger of debts and payments. He refuses to testify unless Odile proves who edited the file. Emotional beat: the ghost made flesh; hope arriving disguised as a demand.

chapters.title: The Edited Page
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. Comparing Lior's handwritten ledger against the firm's archive, Odile identifies the exact hand that altered the report — their own supervisor, Ruth Calloway, who has been laundering the parish hush money through insurance payouts for years. Emotional beat: fury and clarity; the villain wore a lanyard, not a collar.

chapters.title: Offered a File Cabinet
chapters.summary: Calloway, POV. She offers Odile a promotion, a transfer, and a clean version of events — the same deal she gave Bell. Odile pretends to consider while recording nothing, because some things shouldn't be filed. Emotional beat: temptation offered politely; Odile's identity crystallizes in refusal.

chapters.title: Fire Anniversary
chapters.summary: Lior, POV. On the fifth anniversary vigil, the killer strikes again, torching the memorial hall with Lior inside. Odile pulls him out through a window, burned and half-conscious, as the congregation finally sees the boy they mourned. Emotional beat: terror transformed into revelation — the dead witness resurrected before the whole town.

chapters.title: What the Town Knew
chapters.summary: Multiple voices, brief interlocking POVs. Parishioners come forward in a flood: the payments, the affidavits, the night they carried Lior into the crypt to save him from Hale's brother. The conspiracy was communal, protective, and rotten at its bank account. Emotional beat: collective confession; complicity and love in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Trial Begins
chapters.summary: Pruitt and Odile, alternating. Opening day: Calloway's lawyers move to disqualify Odile as a compromised investigator, and the judge nearly agrees until Odile surrenders their badge voluntarily, choosing to testify as a civilian witness. Emotional beat: sacrifice as strategy; Odile burns their career to light the room.

chapters.title: Photographic Testimony
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. On the stand, Odile recites the fire report verbatim — both versions, original and altered — from memory, walking the courtroom through each forged stroke. Calloway breaks on cross-examination when Odile quotes her own words from the bribe meeting. Emotional beat: triumph of the mind as instrument of justice; catharsis.

chapters.title: Verdicts, Old and New
chapters.summary: Pruitt, POV. Hale is acquitted of murder but pleads guilty to obstruction; Calloway is indicted; Hale's brother is arrested for the recent killings. The town reckons with what its kindness concealed. Lior, cleared and legally resurrected, stands in the courthouse doorway unsure where to go. Emotional beat: justice imperfect but real; exhaustion edged with relief.

chapters.title: A Seat at the Table
chapters.summary: Odile, POV, epilogue. Months later, Odile — unemployed, unregretful — helps Lior rebuild the parish records honestly, and the found family sets a place for them at Sunday dinner without being asked. The last line mirrors the first: a coat on a hook, this time freely given. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not inherited; quiet, hard-won peace.
